program: SNAP — Utah has no distinctive local program nickname; DWS's own consumer pages call it plainly "SNAP" or "Food Stamps" (see PROVENANCE.md)
agency: Utah Department of Workforce Services (DWS) — a single agency has administered Utah's SNAP program under this name since a 1997 government reorganization, with no rebrand-lag pattern this pack found (contrast this roster's Oklahoma, Kentucky, and Louisiana findings)
admin_note: Utah is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program, run through a network of DWS Employment Center offices statewide — not county-administered like CA/NY/MN/WI/VA. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FINDING this pack found: Utah's SNAP-specific Administrative Code chapter, Utah Admin. Code R986-900, contains only TWO sections total — R986-900-901 (Authority, which incorporates 7 CFR 271-283 by reference and applies the general R986-100 provisions) and R986-900-902 (Options and Waivers, a short list of state elections). The DETAILED, day-to-day operative SNAP policy instead lives in a separately-published, numbered-chapter online manual — DWS's own "Child Care, Financial and SNAP Eligibility Policy Manual" (jobs.utah.gov/infosource/eligibilitymanual) — rather than in the Administrative Code chapter itself. This is a genuine structural departure from this roster's Oklahoma and Kentucky packs, where the state Administrative Code chapter IS the detailed operative policy source. This pack also found and CONFIRMS a widely-repeated secondary-source claim: Utah has NOT adopted Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) — R986-900-902's own list of adopted federal options does not include a BBCE election, and DWS's own consumer pages and current Table 2 (SNAP Monthly Income Limits, effective 10/1/2025) both publish the plain federal 130%/100% FPL gross/net income tests with no higher percentage-of-FPL band, unlike this roster's Oklahoma, Kentucky, Louisiana, and Alabama BBCE-equivalent packs. Separately, this pack CORRECTS a second widely-repeated secondary-source claim — that Utah counts vehicle value against the resource limit because it lacks BBCE — DWS's own consumer page states plainly that "your car and any other motorized vehicles you own are usually not counted toward the resource limit," and R986-900-902(1)(h) confirms Utah applies its own TANF vehicle-allowance rule in conjunction with the federal SNAP vehicle regulation (7 CFR 273.8) rather than a blanket fair-market-value count. Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DWS Employment Center, the same caution this roster already carries for its other 29 verified states.
system: DWS processes SNAP; applicants apply online through myCase (jobs.utah.gov/mycase), in person at a DWS Employment Center, or by requesting a mailed application. Ordinary processing is the federal default of no later than 30 calendar days; expedited service (very low income/liquid resources, or a destitute migrant/seasonal farmworker household) is the plain federal 7-calendar-day ceiling, stated directly on DWS's own SNAP applicant page — Utah does not accelerate this the way this roster's Kentucky pack found Kentucky does (5 days). Cases are reviewed on a 6-to-12-month cycle generally (DWS's own multi-program Reviews page), with a separate, longer 3-year (36-month) Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) certification period for elderly/disabled households, confirmed directly on DWS's own SNAP requirements page.

verification.method: Direct curl fetch (browser User-Agent) of DWS's own official SNAP eligibility policy manual pages (jobs.utah.gov/infosource/eligibilitymanual/...) — including Table 2 (SNAP Monthly Income Limits and Maximum Assistance Amounts, effective 10/1/2025, current FFY2026 figures), Policy 342 (SNAP Work Requirements, effective 5/1/2026, confirming the current 18-64 ABAWD age range), and Policy 342-1A (Federal Exemptions, effective 2/1/2026) — all clean HTTP 200, HTML-to-text converted. Also directly fetched: DWS's own consumer-facing SNAP pages (deductions.html, requirements.html, index.html, ebt/index.html, reviews/index.html), all clean HTTP 200; the Utah Legislature's own current compiled Utah Code § 35A-3-311 (le.utah.gov, clean HTTP 200, current version effective 5/6/2026); Utah Administrative Code R986-900-901 and R986-900-902 via the Cornell Legal Information Institute's regulatory mirror (clean HTTP 200); USDA FNA's own SNAP Food Restriction Waiver approval letter for Utah (clean HTTP 200, direct PDF-equivalent HTML text) and DWS's own December 2025 press release on the same soft-drink demonstration project; USDA FNA's current Restaurant Meals Program state list and Time Limit (ABAWD) Waivers FY 2025-2029 state-response index (both clean HTTP 200, Utah absent from both). WebSearch cross-checks were used to locate exact manual-chapter URLs before every direct primary-source fetch, and to identify (then reject where unconfirmed, or confirm where independently verified) several widely-repeated secondary-source claims about Utah's BBCE and vehicle-resource-treatment status.
verification.gates: No primary-source host access barrier was encountered during this pack's research — every DWS, Utah Legislature, Cornell LII, and USDA FNA URL cited above returned a clean HTTP 200 to direct curl with a browser User-Agent. The genuine gap this pack found was DISCOVERABILITY, not access: Utah's Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) dollar figure for FFY2026 could not be located on any DWS-hosted public page during this pack's research window, despite Utah Admin. Code R986-900-902(1)(d) confirming DWS uses a MANDATORY Simplified Standard Utility Allowance with three utility standards "updated annually and available upon request" — i.e., DWS's own regulation states these figures exist and are updated annually, but does not itself publish them online in a location this pack could locate; the current DWS eligibility-manual Table numbering scheme (Table 1 = TANF/FEP, Table 2 = SNAP income/allotment) does not appear to include a distinct SUA table at a URL this pack's systematic guessing located. This pack discloses this explicitly as a genuine, checked-for gap (see freshness.json) rather than reusing a stale $376 FY2021 figure this pack found repeated by secondary aggregators, or fabricating a current figure.
